title: Habakkuk Questions Violence and God's Answer
summary_text: Habakkuk cries to the LORD about violence and iniquity, asking why law and justice fail while the wicked surround the righteous. The LORD answers that He is raising the Chaldeans, a fierce nation that takes homes and prisoners and treats its own strength as a god. Habakkuk recognizes that God has appointed them for judgment but asks how the Holy One can tolerate their greater evil. He compares their conquest to catching helpless fish and asks whether their killing without mercy will continue.
key_points: Habakkuk calls for help because violence and iniquity block justice and leave the righteous surrounded.
The LORD says He is raising the Chaldeans, whose swift and cruel forces seize homes and captives.
Habakkuk asks how his holy God can use people more wicked than those they swallow up.
He pictures the conqueror making sacrifices to his net and asks whether his killing without mercy will end.

title: The Righteous Live by Faith as Oppressors Fall
summary_text: As Habakkuk waits, the LORD tells him to record a vision that will come true at its appointed time. The proud are never satisfied, but the righteous live by faith. Warnings announce that plunder, unjust wealth, iniquity, and the drunken humiliation of others will return upon those responsible. The earth will know the LORD's glory, while lifeless idols cannot speak or guide anyone. The passage ends by calling the whole earth to silence before the LORD in His holy temple.
key_points: The LORD tells Habakkuk to record the vision and wait for its certain fulfillment.
The righteous live by faith, unlike the proud conqueror whose appetite never rests.
Plunder, unjust gain, and cities built through iniquity will bring shame rather than security.
Those who make neighbors drunk to expose them will face disgrace and the LORD's cup themselves.
Idols cannot give guidance, but the earth must fall silent before the LORD in His holy temple.

title: Habakkuk Trembles Yet Rejoices in God
summary_text: Habakkuk prays in awe of God's deeds and asks Him to remember mercy amid wrath. He describes the Holy One coming in glory, shaking mountains and nations and marching with weapons through earth and sea. God goes out for His people's salvation and to save His anointed, crushing the wicked enemy. Trembling, Habakkuk waits for distress to reach the invaders. Even if crops and livestock fail completely, he will rejoice in the God of his salvation, who gives him strength like a deer on the heights.
key_points: Habakkuk asks the LORD to renew His deeds and show mercy in His wrath.
The Holy One's glory fills heaven and earth as His approach shakes nations and mountains.
God marches through earth and sea for His people's salvation and to save His anointed from the wicked.
Habakkuk trembles yet waits for the invaders' distress and will rejoice in God even if all food fails.
